Definition: from G1223 and G4982; to save thoroughly, i.e. (by implication or analogy) to cure, preserve, rescue, etc.:--bring safe, escape (safe), heal, make perfectly whole, save.
BiblicalUsage: To save through is to bring safely to the other side, and the form in the text spells the verb with a different vowel than the dictionary entry. The sick are saved by touching the hem of His garment, the sailors are saved through the wreck, and eight souls are saved by water in the days of Noah.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe saving through is the whole story of grace; God does not always keep His people out of the water; He brings them through it, and the ark, the garment, and the broken ship all tell the same tale.
